title: Slow Cooker Beef, Barley & Vegetable Stew
description: Stew beef, barley, potatoes, carrots, and tomatoes simmer into a hearty hands-off dinner using familiar grocery-store ingredients.
substitutions: Use peeled sweet potato instead of white potato.
Use quick-cooking barley only if added during the final hour.
Use frozen sliced carrots if that is what you have.

steps.text: Cook until the beef and barley are tender.

cookSteps.text: Put 1 1/2 pounds beef stew meat, 3 sliced carrots, 2 diced potatoes, 1/2 cup pearl barley, 1 can diced tomatoes with their juices, 4 cups beef broth, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon dried thyme if using into the slow cooker.
Stir, cover, and cook on LOW for about 8 hours, until the beef, vegetables, and barley are tender.
Stir well. If you want a thinner stew, add a splash of hot broth or water. Taste and season with salt and pepper if needed, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Barley thickens the broth as it sits, so add a little water or broth when reheating.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken, Green Beans & Potatoes
description: Chicken thighs, potatoes, and green beans roast together with simple seasonings for a dependable one-pan dinner.
substitutions: Use chicken breast cutlets, checking them earlier for doneness.
Use broccoli florets instead of green beans.
Use baby potatoes halved instead of diced potatoes.

steps.text: Add chicken and green beans and finish roasting.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1 1/2 pounds potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon salt on a large rimmed sheet pan. Roast 15 minutes.

Toss 1 1/2 pounds chicken thighs and 12 ounces green beans with the remaining 1 tablespoon oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1/2 teaspoon paprika, and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Add them to the pan around the potatoes.
Roast 18–20 minutes more, until the chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest part and the potatoes are tender.
Let the chicken rest 3 minutes, then serve with the roasted potatoes and green beans.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat until the chicken is steaming hot throughout.

title: Leftover Meatloaf, Cheddar & Potato Hash
description: Leftover meatloaf and cooked potatoes turn into a crisp cheesy skillet meal instead of another plain reheated plate.
substitutions: Use leftover cooked ground turkey patties instead of meatloaf.
Use cooked sweet potato instead of white potato.
Use frozen corn instead of peas.

steps.text: Add vegetables and melt the cheese.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil or butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 cups diced cooked potatoes and cook 4 minutes, stirring once or twice, until they begin to brown.
Add 1 1/2 cups crumbled cooked meatloaf and up to 1/2 cup frozen peas. Cook 4–5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is steaming hot.
Sprinkle 1/2 cup shredded cheddar over the skillet. Cover for 1 minute, until melted, then serve.

storage: Best made only while the original meatloaf and potatoes are still within their safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate leftovers from the hash up to 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Lemon Sugar Drop Cookies
description: A small pan of soft lemony drop cookies uses ordinary baking staples and no rolling or chilling.
substitutions: Use bottled lemon juice if fresh lemon is not available.
Skip the zest; the cookies will still have a mild lemon flavor.
Use orange juice and zest for an orange version.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Beat 4 tablespoons softened butter with 1/3 cup sugar until creamy. Mix in 1 egg yolk, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1 teaspoon lemon zest if using.
Stir in 3/4 cup flour and 1/4 teaspoon baking soda just until a soft dough forms.
Drop 6 rounded spoonfuls of dough onto a baking sheet, spacing them apart. Bake 9–10 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers still look soft.
Cool on the pan 5 minutes before moving the cookies.

storage: Store covered at room temperature up to 3 days or freeze up to 1 month.
